parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module passes. Both files deal with the HTTP boundary. RequestParser.ts checks untrusted request bodies and query values and pulls typed fields out of them. When a field is missing or has the wrong type, it raises one error type, InvalidRequestError. createApp.ts sets up the Express app: it turns on JSON body parsing, maps routes to controller handlers, and adds the not-found and error middleware. The two files do different jobs, but both belong to the same concern, the HTTP layer, so they are not unrelated. Each rule lives in one place. The "required" and "must be a string" checks exist only in RequestParser. requiredString reuses optionalString instead of repeating the type check. Neither file works around the other's abstractions. The import graph also shows the controllers and errorHandler.ts using RequestParser.ts, which suggests the module's parsing helper is shared as intended. I couldn't see the controller code, so I can't confirm that every controller uses the parser.
